chunks: Whatever is in it from al-Zuhrī, I have narrated it from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Aṣbahānī, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Munqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhrī—whose name is Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihāb—from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام.

key_terms.اسْمُهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ بْنِ شِه: Identification of al-Zuhrī by his full personal name
key_terms.الزُّهْرِيِّ: Al-Zuhrī, the transmitter to whom this chain is being clarified
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicating direct authorial transmission through the stated chain
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا الس: Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, the endpoint of the chain in this report

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain of the narrations from al-Zuhrī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from al-Zuhrī. It is a chain-identification note establishing the route of transmission back to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام.
